quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Leaving the car running in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Quick stops use time and fuel to speed back up. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.

questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or ice appears. These make roads slippery. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will come next.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: Keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle on all sides. This gives you time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles beside you.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is dangerous mainly because it affects your:
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your blood and reaches your brain in 20 to 40 minutes. It damages the parts of your brain that control judgment and driving skill.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road. You should:

options.text: Turn the steering wheel hard to force the vehicle back on the road.
Speed up and gradually steer back onto the road.
Gently brake and slowly turn the steering wheel to return to the road safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly turn the steering wheel to return to the road safely.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down gently with the brakes. At a safe speed, slowly turn back onto the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangle signs:
questions.explanation: Triangle signs pointing down mean yield. Wait until the road is clear and safe before proceeding.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle siren or lights, you must:

options.text: Move to the right side and stop.
Wave the emergency vehicle to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles pass by moving to the right side of the road and stopping. If you are in an intersection, go through it first, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may go if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you are going the wrong way on a one-way street. You risk a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: How do smoking and preparing to smoke affect driving?

options.text: They do not affect driving abilities.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted across traffic lanes?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop. Stay stopped while the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move left. What should you do?

options.text: Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Look in your side mirror for traffic and turn on your signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Always signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it is dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Fatigue while driving is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may seem drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear to be drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to make a drowsy driver alert.

questions.question: What is true about blind spots on larger vehicles?

options.text: They are the same as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The larger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have blind spots near their rears that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: At night, when another vehicle approaches from the opposite direction, your headlights should be:

options.text: On either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle at night. Use low beams to keep everyone on the road safe.

questions.question: What is a common sign of a drunk driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than normal traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: Where may you not park?

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must stay within 12 inches of the side of the road.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you will need more effort to steer. Slow down and pull off the road to stop safely.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and merge at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can watch the traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and merge at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal and merge at the same speed as other traffic. Always yield to existing traffic when entering a roadway.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Do not try to drive around a train.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way paths with a divider between them. Stay to the right.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what is most important?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers of work zones. They are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols and alert drivers that people are working on or near the highway.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they see an animal on the roadway?

options.text: Pass the animal as closely as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass slowly to avoid startling or frightening it.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking to them during driving.
Only watches the car in front of them.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching for items in your car, reading, looking at scenery, or daydreaming while driving. Always scan the road, check your mirrors, and look at your instrument panel regularly. These safe habits will help you stay focused as a driver.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, other drivers must allow for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
The shorter stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
The lower noise level of large vehicles.
The higher speed of large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: When driving near large trucks, other drivers must allow for the longer stopping distance these vehicles need. Smaller vehicles should stay where the truck driver can see them and where they can see the road ahead clearly.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, a driver must:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Let other traffic and pedestrians go first. Only go when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Stop for the train and wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices are off.
